migration.backup_notice: OxideTerm created a one-time snapshot of your pre-2.0 data. It is a recovery copy, not an automatic rollback.
migration.overview_description: OxideTerm 2 is a full desktop rebuild, not a visual refresh. This short tour covers the changes that affect everyday use.
migration.overview_native_description: Rust and GPUI replace the bundled WebView path for a leaner desktop runtime.
migration.overview_cli_description: The old oxt desktop client is replaced by the independent oxideterm command.
migration.overview_visual_description: Motion, surfaces, dialogs, and full-window backgrounds now follow one native design language.
migration.overview_features_description: Telnet, remote desktop, Host Tools, files, editing, and networking are part of one workspace.
migration.gpui_description: The UI, terminal, and backend now share one Rust process and a GPU-rendered surface, removing the browser bridge from the main data path.
migration.gpui_no_webview_description: The desktop no longer ships a WebView application shell or xterm.js terminal path.
migration.gpui_memory_description: Measured idle memory fell from roughly 300 MB in 1.x to just over 100 MB in the current 2.0 build.
migration.gpui_direct_path_description: Terminal bytes update Rust state directly and GPUI renders it without JSON, WebSocket, or Base64 passes.
migration.gpui_shared_runtime_description: Terminal, SFTP, forwarding, editing, and Host Tools can reuse the same node runtime.
migration.visual_title: Motion and visuals now speak one language
migration.visual_description: The native interface adds purposeful transitions and consistent surface behavior while keeping motion fully under your control.
migration.visual_motion_description: Dialogs, tabs, sidebars, toasts, and popovers now use coordinated transitions.
migration.visual_motion_control_description: Choose a motion profile in Appearance settings; Off removes transition delays entirely.
migration.visual_language_description: Shared spacing, elevation, status, focus, and interaction states make workspace surfaces more consistent.
migration.visual_disable_hint: Switch profiles to preview and apply them immediately. You can change this later in Settings → Appearance.
migration.visual_radius_hint: Drag the slider to preview and apply the global corner radius immediately. You can change it later in Settings → Appearance → Layout.
migration.features_description: 2.0 expands connection types and host operations while rebuilding performance-sensitive paths such as SFTP.
migration.features_telnet_description: New native session types cover legacy systems and serial devices.
migration.features_remote_description: Remote desktop sessions now live beside terminal and file workflows.
migration.features_host_tools_description: Monitor resources and work with processes, services, logs, ports, packages, containers, schedules, and tmux.
migration.features_sftp_description: Node-level ownership, parallel queues, archive transfer, short-read recovery, better progress accounting, and resumable stages improve file work.
migration.features_reconnect_description: Short network interruptions can recover the original SSH runtime before replacement is attempted.
migration.features_editor_description: Local file management, previews, project trees, safe writes, conflicts, syntax, and workspace restore are integrated.
migration.internal_description: 2.0 rebuilds ownership, security, packaging, plugins, sync, and recovery around clearer boundaries.
migration.internal_ownership_description: Closing one terminal no longer implicitly destroys unrelated SFTP, forwarding, editing, or Host Tools work.
migration.internal_security_description: russh with ring, strict host keys, OS keychain storage, and explicit secret boundaries replace older transport layers.
migration.internal_plugins_description: Native manifests, Wasm, and process runtimes replace the legacy WebView plugin path.
migration.internal_sync_description: Conflict preview, history, rollback, and user-owned storage backends are now part of the workspace.
migration.internal_updates_description: Signed metadata, checksums, platform packages, backup snapshots, and recovery paths support the 2.0 lifecycle.
migration.internal_platform_description: macOS, Windows, and Linux each receive native window, process, input, packaging, and integration handling.
migration.internal_finish_notice: Your migrated data remains local. Review connections, authentication, plugins, cloud sync, and AI provider settings after entering the workspace.

onboarding.subtitle: Native workspace for remote operations
onboarding.project_intro: OxideTerm is a Rust-native desktop client for authorized remote operations. It keeps terminal sessions, file transfer, tunnels, serial devices, remote desktop, sync, and optional AI assistance under local user control without a bundled browser runtime.
onboarding.highlight_performance_desc: Async I/O, GPUI native rendering, zero-copy binary protocol.
onboarding.highlight_security_arch_desc: OS keychain, ChaCha20 encryption, pure Rust SSH stack.
onboarding.highlight_crossplatform_desc: macOS, Windows, and Linux with a native look and feel.
onboarding.highlight_extensible_desc: Plugin system, custom themes, MCP integration, CLI tool.
onboarding.theme_hint: Pick a terminal color scheme. You can always change this later in Settings.
onboarding.appearance_desc: Customize themes, fonts, motion, and corner radius. You can change them later in Settings.
onboarding.font_hint: Fonts marked ✓ are bundled and ready to use.
onboarding.animation_hint: Choose how much interface motion you prefer.
onboarding.radius_hint: Choose a global corner radius and preview it immediately.
onboarding.workflow_desc: One SSH connection powers your entire workflow.
onboarding.workflow_connect_desc: Add an SSH server with password, key, or certificate authentication.
onboarding.workflow_terminal_desc: Open multiple terminals with tabs and split panes.
onboarding.workflow_sftp_desc: Browse, upload, and download files via the built-in SFTP browser.
onboarding.workflow_forwarding_desc: Set up local, remote, or dynamic (SOCKS5) port forwards.
onboarding.workflow_ide_desc: Edit remote files with syntax highlighting and code completion.
onboarding.quick_start_desc: Get started right away — open a local terminal, connect to a server, or import your existing SSH config.
onboarding.shortcuts_hint: Master these shortcuts to boost your productivity.
onboarding.features_desc: A broader tour of the workspace surfaces available after setup.
onboarding.cmd_palette_desc: Access connections, settings, and themes — one shortcut away.
onboarding.ai_chat_desc: Sidebar chat, inline terminal assistant, and autonomous agent mode — ask questions, generate commands, analyze output.
onboarding.sftp_desc: Browse remote files, drag-and-drop upload/download with transfer queue.
onboarding.port_forwarding_desc: Local, remote, and SOCKS5 dynamic tunnels through SSH.
onboarding.reconnect_desc: 30s grace period — TUI apps like vim stay intact.
onboarding.multiplexing_desc: Terminal, SFTP, port forwarding share one SSH connection.
onboarding.security_desc: Keychain storage, ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption, pure Rust SSH.
onboarding.local_file_manager_desc: Desktop file browser with Quick Look previews, bookmarks, and drag-drop.
onboarding.wsl_graphics_desc: Run Linux GUI apps on Windows via built-in VNC — desktop or single-app mode.
onboarding.plugin_system_desc: Extend with custom tabs, terminal hooks, commands, and settings via WASM plugins.
onboarding.custom_themes_desc: 30+ built-in terminal themes, or create your own with JSON definitions.
onboarding.tip_settings: All settings are customizable — press {{shortcut}} to open Settings anytime.
onboarding.tip_multiplexing: Terminal, SFTP, and port forwarding share a single SSH connection via multiplexing — no extra authentication needed.
onboarding.tip_shortcuts: Press {{shortcut}} anytime to view the full keyboard shortcuts reference.

onboarding.disclaimer_no_warranty_text: OxideTerm is provided "as is", without warranty of any kind. The entire risk as to the quality and performance of the software is with you.
onboarding.disclaimer_data_security_text: You are solely responsible for safeguarding your SSH credentials, private keys, and server configurations. The authors are not liable for data loss, security incidents, or unauthorized access.
onboarding.disclaimer_ai_text: AI-generated outputs are for informational purposes only and do not constitute professional advice. Always review AI-generated commands before execution. Terminal content may be sent to third-party AI providers when enabled.
onboarding.disclaimer_accept: I have read and agree to the above terms
onboarding.disclaimer_gpl_note: Full license and legal terms: GPL-3.0 §15–16 and LEGAL.md.
onboarding.ai_tools_desc: Enable AI-powered features to enhance your terminal workflow.
onboarding.ai_setup_desc: Choose which AI features to enable. You can always change these later in Settings.
onboarding.ai_tools_oxidesens_desc: A built-in AI assistant that understands your terminal context — ask questions, generate commands, analyze output, and automate tasks directly from the sidebar or inline in the terminal.
onboarding.ai_tools_cap_sidebar: Sidebar chat with terminal context awareness
onboarding.ai_tools_cap_inline: Inline terminal assistant for quick commands
onboarding.ai_tools_cap_agent: Autonomous agent mode for complex tasks
onboarding.ai_tools_cap_byok: Bring your own API key — works with any provider
onboarding.ai_tools_privacy_local: All processing happens locally — no data is collected by OxideTerm
onboarding.ai_tools_privacy_keys: API keys are stored securely in your OS keychain
onboarding.ai_tools_privacy_context: Terminal content is sent to your chosen AI provider only when you ask
onboarding.ai_tools_enable_hint: You can change this anytime in Settings → AI.
onboarding.ai_tools_enable_tools_hint: Allow the model to use built-in tools such as file reading, terminal inspection, and approved actions.
onboarding.ai_tools_enable_tools_warning: Tool use is managed separately from chat and remains permission-based. You can review per-tool approvals later in Settings → AI.
onboarding.ai_tools_cmd_palette_desc: Your universal shortcut — quickly access connections, settings, themes, and AI features. Press once to get started.
onboarding.ai_tools_later_hint: All AI and tool settings can be configured later in Settings. No API keys are required during setup.
onboarding.remote_ide_desc: SFTP-backed project tree, multi-tab editing, dirty tracking, and conflict-aware saves.
onboarding.serial_console_desc: Open local serial devices with status controls, line policy, hex mode, Break, DTR, and RTS.
onboarding.remote_desktop_desc: Open remote desktop tabs with reconnect controls, keyboard, mouse, clipboard, and cursor handling.
onboarding.host_tools_desc: Inspect processes, Docker, services, tmux, logs, ports, filesystem state, and host metrics.
onboarding.quick_commands_desc: Save reusable commands by group, search them quickly, and run them from the terminal command bar.
